answer: To resist fake-identity attacks, an AI agent economy enforces proof-of-personhood via tokenized identity bindings. Each agent must stake a unique, unforgeable cryptographic anchor—a synthetic opal token whose scarcity prevents one agent from spawning multiple identities. These staked anchors function as a vine binding distinct agents, nullifying duplicate Sybil entries. Consequently, creating mass fake identities requires purchasing a scarce, non-forgeable material, forcing attackers to pay a prohibitive cost instead of using cheap umber to forge duplicates.
